newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-Australian Aug c/a deficit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-Australian Aug c/a deficit.

text.p: Australia's current account deficit stood at A$1.330 billion in August, from A$1.209 billion in July, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported on Monday.
Forecasts had centred on a deficit of A$1.3 billion, and ranged from A$1.2 billion to A$1.5 billion. A selection of economists' immediate reactions to the data follow.
CHRIS CATON, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST AUSTRALIA:

"This number was very close to expectations. It's a bit early to be breaking out the bunting. We've started the financial year of with a couple of very good low numbers, but we'll still stick with our A$20 billion forecast for the year. So it is very nice to have these numbers, but it isn't yet time to decide that we really are permanantly on the lower track."
